precepts.text: Therefore if any man be in Christ, he is a new creature: old things are passed away; behold, all things are become new. The old man is dead; whatever you were, it is passed away. This is why we take on new names, to symbolize the new man and the new woman; it is not mandatory, but it is an example.
precepts.point: Buried with him in baptism, wherein also ye are risen with him through the faith of the operation of God. Baptism was always symbolic: you are buried in the water as in the grave, and you come up a new creature.

note.label: Deceived by Enticing Words: Colossians 2

precepts.why:
Colossians says we are “risen with him through the faith of the operation of God, who hath raised him from the dead.” Christ came up from the dead, and he is our example, to be like him. “Therefore if any man be in Christ, he is a new creature.” Why? Because you were buried in baptism. The old man is dead. The old woman is dead. The old hoe is dead.

“Old things are passed away.” All the old things you did, whether you were a crackhead, a meth head, an opium user, a fentanyl user, whatever it was, now you clean your system out. For anyone struggling with drugs, there is nothing wrong with getting clinical help; do not sit at home knowing the drug is there and that you are going to use it. There are clinics set up for that. If there are brothers or sisters trained in that field, maybe something can be set up so everything is done legitimately and lawfully. Until then, get the help you need.

“Behold, all things are become new.” This is why we take on new names, to symbolize the new man and the new woman. It is not mandatory, but it is an example. Water baptism was always a symbol of that same thing: the new man and the new woman coming up from the grave as a new person.

precepts.text: For we walk by faith, not by sight. We fear what we physically see, but we do not fear breaking God's commandments. That we should fear.
precepts.point: This is the king. If the king is scared, what is that going to do to the men under him? If the officer is fearful, it spreads to the soldiers under him.

note.label: The Bold and the Bashful

precepts.why:
“For we walk by faith, not by sight.” Christians use that all the time and don’t know what it means. But in this aspect we can use it about fear.

We fear what we see. We don’t fear the Lord; we fear what we physically see. A brother at camp gets unruly with us, he’s got a gun or a knife or whatever, and we fear that. But we don’t fear breaking God’s commandments. That we don’t really fear.

That was Saul. When he “saw the host of the Philistines, he was afraid.” He walked by sight. He feared the Philistines he could see and the people who were scattering from him, but he did not fear transgressing the commandment of the Lord, and it cost him the kingdom.

precepts.text: Knowing the terror of the Lord, we persuade men. The love of Christ constrains us so that we do not live unto ourselves. If we tell the people to come out of the world and do not live it ourselves, we were profitable to many but not to ourselves, and the punishment fits what we knew.
precepts.point: Come out from among them and be ye separate, touch not the unclean thing, and I will receive you and be a father unto you, and ye shall be my sons and daughters.

note.label: Much Is Given, Much Is Required

precepts.why:
“Knowing therefore the terror of the Lord, we persuade men”. We know the terror of the Lord, so we persuade our people to come out of the world. “For the love of Christ constraineth us; because we thus judge, that if one died for all, then were all dead: And that he died for all, that they which live should not henceforth live unto themselves, but unto him which died for them, and rose again.”

He made him to bear our sins. So did God send his Son to die so we could keep sinning in hypocrisy? He sent Christ to die for our sins, gave us his laws, and made us friends, prophets and ambassadors. That is why chapter 6 opens “We then, as workers together with him, beseech you also that ye receive not the grace of God in vain.” Let this word be profitable to you, so that you become prophets of God, the women bear prophets back on the earth, and the daughters are righteous.

We do not live unto ourselves. If we tell the people to come out of the world and do not live it ourselves, we were profitable to many but not to ourselves, and the punishment fits what we knew. Much is given, and much is required.

So this is our life. There is no other life outside of this: no friends in the world, nobody else to call. If you have another life where you feel comfortable, you have not been in the truth. The love of Christ constrains us to live unto him.

precepts.text: Knowing therefore the terror of the Lord, the King of terrors of Job, we persuade men. We are the watchmen who know what he will do, so we must persuade our people in the midst of all kinds of sin, and we must be studying so that we can help them. The whole head is sick, and we learn to discipline ourselves and persuade our people to change.
precepts.point: The burden of Babylon which Isaiah saw: lift ye up a banner upon the high mountain, the government, America; the banner is the Bible. Exalt the voice unto them, as Isaiah 58:1 says lift it up like a trumpet and spare not, and shake the hand, warn our people, that they may go into the gates of the nobles. In the midst of the war Isaiah sees the prophets still going out.

note.label: America At War With Iran: Preparation For Conflict

precepts.why:
Isaiah sees the war coming on Babylon and the prophets still lifting up the banner and exalting the voice. Paul says why we do it: “Knowing therefore the terror of the Lord, we persuade men.” In Job he is called the king of terrors. We know what the Lord is going to do. The Lord set us up as watchmen, and since we know the terror of the Lord, we must persuade men.

“But we are made manifest unto God; and I trust also are made manifest in your consciences.”

Who are we trying to persuade? Our people, in the midst of all kinds of sin. So brothers, we must be studying, so that when we come across our people we are able to help them. The scripture says the whole head is sick: we are sick individuals ourselves. But we must learn to discipline ourselves, and we must learn how to persuade our people to change their lives.

precepts.text: I have espoused you to one husband, to present you as a chaste virgin to Christ.
precepts.point: Paul espoused Israel as a chaste virgin to one husband, Christ.

note.label: Transforming from Immorality into Beautiful Civility Part 2

precepts.why:
“For I am jealous over you with godly jealousy: for I have espoused you to one husband”. The espousal was made when the Most High sent his son Christ, because Christ died for us, his woman. We are the woman of the Most High. We are men physically, but we are his bride, and that is why Paul uses that term.

He cleaned us up. Sanctified them through thy truth; thy word is truth. Once he cleaned us up, we became virgins with him: “that I may present you as a chaste virgin to Christ.” That is crystal clear. It is what 2 Corinthians 5:17 means: “if any man be in Christ, he is a new creature: old things are passed away”.

There is such a thing as history, but your history only comes up if you keep doing what you used to do. Then it becomes a blot on your record today. None of us was born in this truth, so whatever you sisters went through, and the same with you brothers, clean yourselves up while you are here. All of us have a chance to get ourselves correct.

Once the slate is cleaned, we do not dirty it up. We do not defile it or mess it up. That is how we stay a chaste virgin espoused to Christ.

precepts.text: They were redeemed from among men, the firstfruits unto God and to the Lamb.
precepts.point: Paul espoused Israel as a chaste virgin to one husband, Christ.

note.label: Transforming from Immorality into Beautiful Civility Part 2

precepts.why:
“These are they which were not defiled with women; for they are virgins.” That does not necessarily mean they are virgins physically. They are virgins in this truth. They put off the weak nature, the sins and the cares of the world. They are the ones that came in and repented, the new creature of 2 Corinthians 5:17, where old things are passed away and all things are become new.

“These are they which follow the Lamb whithersoever he goeth. These were redeemed from among men”: redeemed from among the filth. To be redeemed means you were in the filth, in the vomit, at a serious deficit, and you had to be brought up out of it. We were redeemed from that, “being the firstfruits unto God and to the Lamb.” We have been cleaned up for the Lord, men and women, so we have a chance and an opportunity to get it right.

“And in their mouth was found no guile”: no lies, “for they are without fault before the throne of God.” How can that be? Only when you are keeping the commandments of God and the faith of Christ.

So watch how you move. Replay your own actions in your mind, see how you are operating, and catch yourself, because there is an effort to take us off our path. The virgins who follow the Lamb keep the slate clean.

precepts.text: We have a building of God, an house not made with hands, eternal in the heavens.
precepts.point: The angel who spoke to John called himself his fellow servant and his brother.

note.label: The Kingdom Of Adam And The Old World

precepts.why:
Before the world was made, everyone obeyed, because we were not in the flesh. Paul shows the body we had and will have again: “For we know that if our earthly house of this tabernacle were dissolved, we have a building of God, an house not made with hands, eternal in the heavens.” If this body is dissolved, we have a body, not made with hands like Adam formed of the dust of the ground, but eternal in the heavens: a celestial body.

“For in this we groan, earnestly desiring to be clothed upon with our house which is from heaven”. We groan in this body because it is susceptible to sin, and we want our body from heaven. “If so be that being clothed we shall not be found naked.” That is what Adam's nakedness was: not running around naked, but being in the flesh. Before, he had a spiritual body; God took his spirit and put it in the flesh. That nakedness is the shame, the sinful nature.

We groan “not for that we would be unclothed, but clothed upon, that mortality might be swallowed up of life.” We want our immortal body. “we walk by faith, not by sight”, “willing rather to be absent from the body, and to be present with the Lord.”

So when you die keeping the commandments, you are present with the Lord. This is for every brother and sister who is sick, who has been told they do not have long to live, and for those who have passed away: we understand where they are. Don't be afraid. Conquer that fear. If you did what was right on this earth and dealt right with the saints, absent from this body, you will be with the Lord.

precepts.text: If any man be in Christ, he is a new creature; old things are passed away, and a vow made while serving the world does not stand.
precepts.point: Swearing on the Bible in the court system is another matter: be subject unto the higher powers, for the powers that be are ordained of God, and you also have the option to affirm; either way, tell the truth.

note.label: Numbers 30: The Law of Vows

precepts.why:
What about a vow made before you came into this truth? “Therefore if any man be in Christ, he is a new creature: old things are passed away; behold, all things are become new.”

A vow made while serving the world does not stand, for you were not vowing to the God of Israel then. Old things are passed away; the man who comes into Christ is a new creature, and the promises of the old man are not bound on the new.

precepts.text: The love of Christ constraineth us from sin.
precepts.point: We are the church of the living God, the pillar and ground of the truth, and we must learn to behave ourselves and possess our vessels, constrained from sin.

note.label: Isaiah 33: The Lord Our Judge, Lawgiver, and King

precepts.why:
The Most High “hath filled Zion with judgment and righteousness”, and we who are the church of the living God must learn to behave ourselves and possess our vessels. What holds us back from sin? “For the love of Christ constraineth us; because we thus judge, that if one died for all, then were all dead”.

The love of Christ constraineth us from sin. Because he died for all, we judge that we were all dead, and so we are held in, constrained, from the sin that made us dead. That constraint is the fear of the Lord that is his treasure, and it is how we possess our vessels as the pillar and ground of the truth.

precepts.text: We must all appear before the judgment seat of Christ.
precepts.point: He that heareth my word, and believeth on him that sent me, hath everlasting life, and shall not come into condemnation.

note.label: John 5: The Pool of Bethesda and the Witness to the Son

precepts.why:
“For the Father judgeth no man, but hath committed all judgment unto the Son”. That is why men stand before the judgment seat of Christ: “For we must all appear before the judgment seat of Christ; that every one may receive the things done in his body, according to that he hath done, whether it be good or bad.”

All judgment is committed unto the Son, so the judgment seat is Christ's, and every one receives there the things done in his body, good or bad. That is also why “all men should honour the Son, even as they honour the Father.”
